briefing_2026-10-13_tahmo_kenya_cities_r: Station rainfall over the past month was heaviest in the second half of September, with daily peaks of about 32 mm at Eldoret on 17 September, 33 mm at Mombasa on 19 September, 28 to 30 mm at Kisumu on 19 and 24 September and 37 mm at Nakuru on 23 September. Early October was quieter, with daily totals below 10 mm at all five stations, before renewed falls of about 17 mm at Mombasa on 10 October and 28 mm at Eldoret on 11 October. Nairobi stayed nearly dry throughout, never exceeding about 5 mm in a day.
briefing_2026-10-13_tahmo_kenya_cities_t: Daily mean temperatures over the past month were steady at Mombasa (25 to 27 C) and clearly lower inland, with Kisumu at 19 to 22 C and a peak near 24 C on 4 October, and Nakuru and Eldoret at 15 to 19 C. Nairobi warmed gradually from 16 to 18 C in mid September to about 20 C in early October. All five stations show a sharp drop on the last day plotted, 13 October, which should be treated with caution.
briefing_2026-10-13_kenya_weekly_rainfal: Observed CHIRPS rainfall over Kenya stayed at 2 to 9 mm per week from early August to early October 2026, close to the analog years 2006, 2015 and 2023 and well below 2019, which had already climbed to 40 to 58 mm by early October. The downscaled S2S ensemble mean from the 11 October run gives about 23 mm per week for the two weeks from mid October, rising to 28 mm and then about 38 mm in the week starting in early November. The one-sigma range widens from roughly 14 to 34 mm at the start to 14 to 63 mm by early November, with individual members between about 5 and more than 90 mm, and the mean tracks the 2006 and 2015 analogs rather than the 2023 peak near 97 mm.
briefing_2026-10-13_kenya_ecmwf_chirps_v: For the week of 28 September to 4 October, CHIRPS observed less than 10 mm over most of Kenya, with 20 to 30 mm only in the west near 1.5N, while ECMWF S2S forecast more widespread totals of 10 to 30 mm at all four lead weeks. Against the 5 mm threshold the forecasts scored hits in the west along the equator, in the east along the Somali border and on the south coast at every lead. Central and southern Kenya were false alarms at week 1 (init 28 September), week 2 and week 4, and the week-3 forecast (init 14 September) verified best, so the shorter leads gave no extra confidence for this week.
briefing_2026-10-13_kenya_ecmwf_chirps_b: ECMWF S2S was too wet over most of Kenya for the week of 28 September to 4 October, with forecast minus CHIRPS biases of +5 to +18 mm across the centre and east. The wet bias was largest at week 1 (init 28 September) and week 2 (init 21 September), reaching +15 to +18 mm in the northeast between 2N and 4N and in the south-centre and on the south coast. The only dry bias, -15 to -20 mm, sat in the western cell near 1.5N where CHIRPS observed 20 to 30 mm, and the week-3 forecast (init 14 September) had the smallest errors overall.
